newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi denies alliance with GM in India.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi denies alliance with GM in India.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp on Wednesday denied a Japanese newspaper report that it would consign production of its compact car in India to General Motors Corp.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Wednesday that GM would produce a Mitsubishi passenger car at GM India, GM's Indian joint venture with Hindustan Motors Ltd, a major Indian carmaker, from early 1998.

"The story is not correct. Simply, Hindustan will utilise GM India, its 50-50 venture with GM, to start assembling Mitsubishi's Lancer in 1998. It is not an alliance between Mitsubishi and GM, it's between Hindustan and GM India," a Mitsubishi spokesman said.
Hindustan will move the assembly of the Lancers to a new plant when it is completed in the next two or three years, the spokesman said.
It originally plans to produce 10,000 of the cars a year. They will be sold in India by Hindustan with Mitsubishi's badge.
Mitsubishi has no capital investment in Hindustan or GM India.
